사이.x: The bank is between the post office and the hospital.
사이.e: Also means relationship: 사이가 좋다 = to get along well.
사이.t: Pattern: A와/하고 B 사이에 = between A and B. Often shortened to 새 in speech.

돌아오다.ex: 아버지는 저녁 일곱 시에 집에 돌아와요.
돌아오다.x: My father comes back home at seven in the evening.
돌아오다.e: 돌다 (turn) + 오다 (come) — 'turn and come back'; pairs with 돌아가다.

기자.ex: 기자들이 유명한 배우에게 질문을 많이 했어요.
기자.x: The reporters asked the famous actor a lot of questions.
기자.e: -자 = person who does it: 기자, 과학자, 운전자.

실패하다.ex: 한 번 실패해도 다시 하면 돼요.
실패하다.x: Even if you fail once, you can just try again.

자연.x: I want to enjoy beautiful nature in the countryside.
자연.e: Literally 'so by itself' — things as they naturally are.
자연.t: 자연스럽다 means 'natural' as in not awkward: 자연스러운 한국어 'natural Korean'.

주름.ex: 할머니는 웃을 때 눈가에 주름이 생겨요.
주름.x: Wrinkles form around my grandmother's eyes when she smiles.
주름.e: Used for skin and for fabric: 주름치마 is a pleated skirt.

사건.ex: 경찰이 그 사건을 아직 조사하고 있어요.
사건.x: The police are still investigating that incident.
사건.e: Literally 'matter item': a case to deal with.
사건.t: Pronounced [사껀]. 사건 is an incident, often criminal; 사고 is an accident like a car crash.

재해.x: I prepared an emergency bag in case of natural disasters.

부정적.ex: 너무 부정적인 생각은 건강에 안 좋아요.
부정적.x: Overly negative thoughts are bad for your health.
부정적.t: Homonym warning: 부정 (不正) also means 'injustice, cheating', as in 부정행위.

할부.x: I bought a laptop on a twelve-month installment plan.
할부.t: At Korean checkouts you'll hear 일시불로 하시겠어요, 할부로 하시겠어요? — 'one payment or installments?'

전달.x: I passed the teacher's message on to my classmates.

단골.ex: 이 떡집은 우리 엄마 단골 가게예요.
단골.x: This rice cake shop is my mom's regular place.
단골.e: Native word. It first meant the shaman a family always called on (단골무당), then a regular customer or shop.
단골.t: 단골 can mean the person (단골손님) or the place (단골집). Regulars often get a little extra for free, called 서비스 or 덤.

귀신.ex: 밤에 그 학교에서 귀신을 봤다는 소문이 있어요.
귀신.x: There's a rumor that someone saw a ghost at that school at night.
귀신.t: The classic Korean ghost is a long-haired woman in white (처녀귀신). 귀신같이 means 'uncannily': 귀신같이 알아요 'knows it uncannily well'.

검토.x: Review the contract carefully before you sign it.

견해.ex: 그 문제에 대해 전문가들의 견해가 달라요.
견해.x: Experts have different views on the issue.
견해.e: Literally 'seeing and understanding': how you see something.
견해.t: 견해 is more formal than 의견; common in 견해를 밝히다 'to state one's view'.

타박상.ex: 다행히 큰 부상은 없고 가벼운 타박상만 입었어요.
타박상.x: Luckily there was no serious injury, just minor bruises.

대선.ex: 다음 대선에서 누구에게 투표할지 아직 모르겠어요.
대선.x: I still don't know who to vote for in the next presidential election.
대선.t: News loves short forms: 총선 (parliamentary), 지방 선거 (local).

안심되다.m: to be relieved, to feel reassured
안심되다.ex: 선생님 말씀을 들으니까 이제 좀 안심돼요.
안심되다.x: Now that I've heard what the doctor said, I feel a bit relieved.
안심되다.e: 안심 'peace of mind' + 되다 'to become' — relief that comes over you.
안심되다.t: 안심되다 is relief caused by something; 안심하다 is often used as a command: 안심하세요.

덜다.forms: 덜어요 · 덜었어요 · 덜 거예요 · 더세요 (ㄹ drops)
덜다.m: to take some off, to remove a portion; to lessen, to ease
덜다.x: There was too much rice, so I took some off.
덜다.t: Common pairs: 부담을 덜다 'ease a burden', 걱정을 덜다 'worry less'.

간절하다.e: Literally 'sincere and urgent' — a wish you feel deep inside.
간절하다.t: Very common as the adverb 간절히: 간절히 바라다, 간절히 원하다.

친밀하다.ex: 우리 가족은 서로 아주 친밀한 관계예요.
친밀하다.x: Our family members have a very close relationship with each other.

조짐.x: There are signs that the economy will recover.
조짐.e: Literally 'omen and sign': an early hint of what's coming.
조짐.t: Usual pattern: -(으)ㄹ 조짐이 보이다 'to show signs of ~'.

품절.x: Those shoes are already sold out.
품절.t: 품절 is for goods; for tickets and seats, 매진 is more common.

선녀.x: A fairy came down from the sky and bathed.
선녀.e: Literally 'immortal woman': a heavenly maiden of Taoist-flavored folklore.
선녀.t: Best known from the tale 선녀와 나무꾼 'The Fairy and the Woodcutter'. 선녀 같다 praises a woman as graceful and beautiful.

엉금엉금.x: The turtle is crawling slowly across the sand.
엉금엉금.e: 의태어 (manner word) for crawling slowly on hands and knees or on four legs.
엉금엉금.t: Pronounced [엉그멍금]: the ㅁ batchim links to the next vowel. Almost always paired with 기다 'to crawl'.

사면.x: The president announced a special pardon on Liberation Day.
사면.t: Homonym: 사면 (四面) means 'all four sides', as in 사면초가.

진리.ex: 과학은 자연의 진리를 찾아가는 하나의 과정이에요.
진리.x: Science is a process of seeking the truth about nature.
진리.t: Pronounced [질리] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

고대.ex: 고대 이집트 사람들은 거대한 피라미드를 만들었어요.
고대.x: The ancient Egyptians built huge pyramids.
고대.e: Literally 'the old era'. Also a nickname for Korea University.

여운.ex: 영화가 끝난 후에도 긴 여운이 남았어요.
여운.x: A long lingering feeling stayed with me even after the movie ended.
여운.e: Literally 'remaining resonance', like a bell that keeps ringing.

문인.m: writer, literary figure, man of letters
문인.ex: 이 카페는 옛날 문인들이 자주 모이던 곳이에요.
문인.x: This café is where writers used to gather in the old days.

처치.ex: 다친 사람에게 빨리 응급 처치를 해야 해요.
처치.x: You have to give first aid to the injured person quickly.
처치.e: Literally 'dealing with and placing' — handling a situation.

만연하다.m: to be widespread, to be rampant, to spread
만연하다.ex: 사회 전반에 불신이 만연해 있다는 지적이 나옵니다.
만연하다.x: Some point out that distrust is widespread throughout society.
만연하다.e: Literally 'vines spreading' — something bad creeping everywhere.
만연하다.t: Pronounced [마년하다]. Usually for negative things: 부정부패, 불신, 전염병.

기이하다.ex: 밤마다 집 근처에서 기이한 소리가 들려요.
기이하다.x: Every night I hear strange sounds near my house.

반항적.ex: 사춘기가 되면서 아들이 점점 반항적으로 변했어요.
반항적.x: As he hit puberty, my son became more and more rebellious.

일괄.m: lump sum, bundle; doing all at once
일괄.ex: 서류는 다음 주에 일괄 처리할 예정입니다.
일괄.x: The documents will be processed all together next week.
일괄.t: Mostly used before another noun: 일괄 처리 'batch processing', 일괄 구매 'bulk purchase'.

차곡차곡.m: neatly piled, layer by layer; bit by bit
차곡차곡.ex: 매달 월급의 일부를 차곡차곡 모으고 있어요.
차곡차곡.x: I'm steadily saving part of my salary every month.
차곡차곡.e: Mimetic word for things stacked neatly one on another.

사면초가.m: being surrounded by enemies on all sides, a hopeless situation
사면초가.ex: 그 회사는 경영 위기로 사면초가에 빠졌습니다.
사면초가.x: The company is cornered on all sides by its management crisis.
사면초가.e: From a Chinese legend: a trapped general heard his homeland's songs from enemies on every side.

조삼모사.m: a trick using a superficial difference; fooling people with the same deal repackaged
조삼모사.ex: 할인이라고 하지만 가격을 따져 보면 조삼모사예요.
조삼모사.x: They call it a discount, but if you do the math it's the same deal in disguise.
조삼모사.e: From a tale: monkeys angry at three nuts at dawn, four at dusk, cheered when it was swapped.

적재적소.m: the right person in the right place
적재적소.x: It's important to put talented people where they fit best.
적재적소.t: Pronounced [적째적쏘]; nearly always 적재적소에 배치하다 or 활용하다.

빈틈.ex: 그 사람은 일 처리에 빈틈이 없어요.
빈틈.x: That person handles work without any slip-ups.
빈틈.e: 빈 'empty' (from 비다) + 틈 'gap' — an empty gap.
빈틈.t: 빈틈없다 is a compliment: 빈틈없는 사람 'a meticulous person'.

국경선.ex: 두 나라는 국경선 문제로 오랫동안 갈등을 겪었습니다.
국경선.x: The two countries have long been in conflict over their border.

하수.ex: 하수가 강으로 흘러가지 않도록 처리해야 해요.
하수.x: Sewage must be treated so it doesn't flow into the river.
하수.e: Literally 'down water' — water that goes down the drain.
하수.t: Homonym warning: 하수 (下手) also means 'a low-skilled player', the opposite of 고수.

그린벨트.ex: 정부가 일부 그린벨트를 풀어서 아파트를 짓기로 했어요.
그린벨트.x: The government decided to lift some greenbelt restrictions to build apartments.
그린벨트.e: From English 'greenbelt'; in Korea it's the official term for development-restricted zones around cities.

정정 보도.ex: 신문사는 잘못된 기사에 대해 정정 보도를 냈습니다.
정정 보도.x: The newspaper published a correction for the inaccurate article.

두둔하다.m: to take someone's side, to stick up for, to defend (often unfairly)
두둔하다.ex: 아버지는 늘 막내만 두둔해서 형이 서운해했어요.
두둔하다.x: Dad always took the youngest's side, so the older brother felt hurt.
두둔하다.e: Its syllables don't help; think of it as 'covering for' someone.
두둔하다.t: Often implies biased defense of someone at fault, unlike principled 옹호하다.

자가 진단 키트.forms: 자가 진단 키트가 · 자가 진단 키트를
자가 진단 키트.ex: 목이 아파서 자가 진단 키트로 검사해 봤어요.
자가 진단 키트.x: My throat hurt, so I tested myself with a home test kit.
자가 진단 키트.t: Sold at pharmacies and convenience stores. Two lines (두 줄) means positive. The official term is 자가 검사 키트.

갓생.m: productive, disciplined life; living a model life
갓생.ex: 올해는 일찍 일어나서 갓생 살 거예요.
갓생.x: This year I'm going to get up early and live a productive life.
갓생.t: Casual/online slang among young people for routines like waking early, exercising and studying. Usually 갓생(을) 살다.

재무제표.ex: 투자하기 전에 회사의 재무제표를 꼼꼼히 확인하세요.
재무제표.x: Check a company's financial statements carefully before you invest.

반세계화.ex: 정상회의장 밖에서 대규모 반세계화 시위가 열렸습니다.
반세계화.x: A large anti-globalization protest was held outside the summit venue.

구조주의.ex: 구조주의는 언어학에서 시작되어 인류학과 철학으로 퍼졌습니다.
구조주의.x: Structuralism began in linguistics and spread to anthropology and philosophy.

자유의지.ex: 인간에게 정말 자유의지가 있는지는 오래된 철학적 질문이에요.
자유의지.x: Whether humans really have free will is an old philosophical question.
자유의지.t: Also often written with a space, 자유 의지; both spellings appear.

도리.m: duty, the right thing to do; way, means
도리.ex: 어른을 공경하는 것은 사람의 도리라고 생각해요.
도리.x: I think respecting your elders is a person's moral duty.
도리.t: Common patterns: 자식 된 도리 (one's duty as a child); 어쩔 도리가 없다 (there's nothing one can do).

신비주의.ex: 그 배우는 신비주의 전략으로 사생활을 공개하지 않아요.
신비주의.x: That actor keeps their private life hidden as a strategy of mystique.
신비주의.t: In K-pop and celebrity news, 신비주의 means deliberately keeping a mysterious, private image.

편집증.ex: 그는 누군가 자기를 감시한다는 편집증에 시달렸어요.
편집증.x: He suffered from paranoia that someone was watching him.
편집증.t: Don't confuse it with 편집 (editing); 편집증 always means paranoia.

플라시보.x: The doctor used sugar pills as a placebo.
플라시보.e: From English 'placebo'; in Korean it appears most often in 플라시보 효과.

말기.x: He was diagnosed with terminal cancer.

비뇨기과.x: I went to urology for a urination problem.
비뇨기과.t: Officially renamed 비뇨의학과, but most people still say 비뇨기과.

유전자 가위.forms: 유전자 가위로 + noun + 을/를 편집하다 (edit ... with gene scissors)
유전자 가위.ex: 과학자들은 유전자 가위로 병을 일으키는 유전자를 고쳤어요.
유전자 가위.x: Scientists fixed a disease-causing gene using gene-editing tools.
유전자 가위.e: 유전자 'gene' + native 가위 'scissors' — a nickname for gene-editing technology.

미문.x: That writer is famous for ornate, elegant prose.
미문.e: Literally 'beautiful writing' — sometimes hints at style over substance.

저술.ex: 그 교수는 은퇴 후에도 활발하게 저술 활동을 하고 있어요.
저술.x: That professor is still actively writing books after retiring.

내시.ex: 내시는 왕의 곁에서 궁궐의 여러 일을 돌보았어요.
내시.x: Eunuchs took care of many palace duties at the king's side.

고매하다.m: lofty, noble, exalted (of character or ideals)
고매하다.x: Everyone respected the teacher's noble character.
고매하다.t: Mostly in set phrases praising others: 고매한 인품, 고매한 뜻.

준엄하다.ex: 국민들은 선거를 통해 준엄한 심판을 내렸습니다.
준엄하다.x: Through the election, the people delivered a stern verdict.
준엄하다.t: News collocations: 준엄한 심판, 준엄한 경고 'a stern verdict/warning'.

문화지체.ex: 기술 발전을 제도가 따라가지 못하면 문화지체가 생깁니다.
문화지체.x: When institutions can't keep up with technological progress, cultural lag occurs.
문화지체.e: Literally 'culture delayed': values and rules lag behind new technology.

차차.forms: 차차 + change verb: 차차 나아지다 · 차차 알게 되다
차차.m: gradually, little by little; later, in due time
차차.ex: 삼월이 되니 날씨가 차차 따뜻해지고 있어요.
차차.x: Now that it's March, the weather is gradually getting warmer.
차차.e: Literally 'next and next' — step by step.
차차.t: Also means 'later': 그 얘기는 차차 하자 'Let's talk about that later.'

황급히.ex: 그는 전화를 받고 황급히 밖으로 나갔어요.
황급히.x: He took the call and rushed outside in a hurry.
황급히.t: Pronounced [황그피] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

세로토닌.ex: 햇빛을 쬐면 세로토닌 분비가 늘어난다고 해요.
세로토닌.x: They say getting sunlight increases serotonin secretion.
nb: 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다
서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊는다
